extracts.text:
8. The Registrar, Tamil Nadu National Law University when requested to state as to whether any direction has been issued by the Central Government authorities or by the Consortium of National Law Universities or under any enactment, rules or regulations to follow any particular reservation policy in respect of seats allotted to All India Category in the admission of National Law Universities, had replied that the National Commission for Backward Classes alone has recommended to provide 27% reservation to OBCs under All India Category seats.

9. In respect of admission of students under All India category, there is no direction by any lawful authority to the National Law Universities to follow only the Central Scheme of reservation. The Central Scheme of reservation which is otherwise enforced by the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 (Central Act 5 of 2007) will apply only to certain Central Educational Institutions established, maintained or aided by the Central Government and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

10. The Tamil Nadu National Law University being a University constituted by the Government of Tamil Nadu under the State enactment and funded by the State Government, there is no legal obligation to follow the Central Scheme of reservation. The surrender of seats to All India category is only an arrangement between the members of Consortium of National Law Universities to become a member of the Said Consortium. There is no instruction or guideline framed by the Consortium with regard to reservation policy to be followed in the admission of National Law Universities.

11. This being the position, it is considered that it is open for the State Government to direct the Tamil Nadu National Law University to follow the State reservation policy in the lines of the reservation mandated by the Tamil Nadu Backward Classes, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Service under the State) Act, 1993 (Tamil Nadu Act 45 of 1994) for the All India category also and there is no legal impediment to do so. If the Tamil Nadu State’s reservation policy is followed in All India category in the admission of students to Tamil Nadu National Law University, it would be more than the percentage of reservation already given for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in All India category and would very well comply with the directions of National Commission for Backward Classes also.
